newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG SHOWS CLASS ON ICY PISTE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG SHOWS CLASS ON ICY PISTE.

text.p: Sweden's world champion Pernilla Wiberg showed her class on an icy piste as some of her rivals came to grief in the first leg of a women's World Cup slalom on Sunday.
Wiberg, the overall World Cup leader, displayed composure and rhythm on a difficult course to clock the fastest time of 46.82 seconds, according to unofficial results.
The Swede held a lead of 0.82 of a second over Austria's Elfi Eder (47.64), with New Zealand's Claudia Riegler clocking the third fastest time of 48.21.
Some of the other top racers found the conditions treacherous.
Slovenia's world bronze medallist Urska Hrovat fell after crossing her skis, while experienced Austrian Anita Wachter and Swiss Karin Roten also lost control and missed gates.
The second leg was due to take place at 1130 GMT.
